Practice reviewing three fictional editorial briefs, with seven fields: source, audience, purpose, deadline, style rules, evidence status, and approval arrangement; 'to be verified' means recorded but unconfirmed, and only unrecorded items count as missing. A: source A; audience A; purpose A; deadline Wednesday; style A; evidence to be verified; approval referred to the responsible editor, 0 missing. B: source not recorded; audience B; purpose B; deadline Friday; style not recorded; evidence to be verified; approval referred to the responsible editor, 2 missing. C: source C; audience C; purpose C; deadline Thursday; style C; evidence verified; approval referred to the designated publisher, 0 missing. Answers 0/2/0; review only the fields and do not publish content.

China's Copyright Law, 2020 revision: Article 10 covers the rights of attribution/modification/integrity; Article 24 provides that use meeting specific statutory conditions may be exempt from permission and payment, but must attribute the work and must not affect normal use or unreasonably prejudice the rights holder. Articles 26/29 cover license contracts and the boundary of rights not expressly licensed; Article 36 provides that modification or abridgement of books requires the author's permission, while textual modification or abridgement in newspapers and periodicals may be carried out according to law and content modification requires the author's permission. Not all textual changes require separate approval, and citation or institutional consent does not acquire all copyright. Editorial suggestion: confirm the applicable license or statutory exception, do not rely on material when permission is unclear, and do not treat every missing authorization as infringement.

China's designated publishing units' publishing professional and technical positions are subject to the National Press and Publication Administration regulation: Article 2 covers editing/proofreading in book, non-news periodical, audio-visual, electronic, and online publishing units and proofreading in newspapers and news periodicals; Article 4 requires obtaining the publishing professional qualification and registering within 2 years of taking the post, and responsible editors must be at intermediate level or above, registered, and certified before taking the post. Article 5 provides for the qualification registration of publishing unit presidents, editors-in-chief, chief editors, and editorial office directors (including deputies). Editing and reporting in newspapers/news periodicals and editing and proofreading for ethnic minority publications are separately regulated under Article 32 and cannot be extended to a uniform threshold for all self-media/enterprise content editors. Articles 14/16 distinguish qualification registration from responsible editor registration, and institutional authorization cannot replace statutory qualifications.
